name: Synthetic diagram styles
description: Six invented examples inspired by the selected architecture excerpts, varying topology, semantic perspective, detail, and notation.
usageGuidance: These examples describe invented software systems. Use them only as demonstrations of representational choices, never as source evidence for a target system. Match the actual evidence when choosing labels, depth, branching, density, and relationships. The examples deliberately differ: some are shallow, some expand selectively; some use [M]/[O]/[C]/[D], others need no tags. Do not impose all four relationship types, public/private sections, error branches, shared-result markers, or lifecycle phases on every diagram. Shared-result references, retry arrows, and event siblings have explicit meanings; reuse those devices only when supported. Branch order implies sequence only when the labels explicitly say so. These are output-style references, not paired source-to-diagram demonstrations. Treat this set as a pool: choose a small, complementary subset for a prompt rather than always including all six. Selection diversity is an authoring judgment, not a measured reduction in model overfitting.

examples.title: Shallow dispatch
examples.diversityRationale: Broad and shallow; parallel alternatives need no invented internal hierarchy.
examples.ascii:
decode(mediaType, bytes)
|-- application/json -> JSON value
|-- text/csv         -> rows keyed by header
|-- image/png        -> pixel buffer + dimensions
`-- anything else    -> UnsupportedMediaType

examples.title: Shared dependency
examples.diversityRationale: Result-first dependency tree; names shared intermediate results explicitly instead of implying exclusive ownership.
examples.ascii:
[D] Search response
|-- page of matches
|   |-- ranked matches
|   |   |-- matching document IDs [shared A]
|   |   |   `-- query terms + inverted index
|   |   `-- scoring weights + document statistics
|   `-- offset + page size
`-- total matches
    `-- count([shared A])
        `-- same IDs; no second matching pass

examples.title: Resource lifetime
examples.diversityRationale: Temporal phases distinguish ownership from borrowing; a short call path sits inside an asymmetric lifecycle tree.
examples.ascii:
[O] Connection lease
|-- Acquire
|   `-- pool lends one connection to one request
|       `-- pool retains ownership; request gets exclusive use
|-- While borrowed
|   |-- [C] begin -> execute statements -> commit
|   `-- statement or commit fails -> attempt rollback
`-- Release on every exit
    |-- healthy connection -> return to idle pool
    `-- broken connection -> close and remove from pool
        `-- later acquisition may create a replacement

examples.title: Bounded retry
examples.diversityRationale: Outcome branches, a terminal failure, and a bounded back-reference express control flow without recursively expanding a loop.
examples.ascii:
[C] Deliver webhook                         at most 3 attempts
`-- POST event with stable delivery ID
    |-- 2xx -> mark delivered
    |-- permanent rejection -> mark failed
    `-- timeout / temporary rejection
        |-- attempts remain
        |   `-- wait with backoff -> retry POST above
        |       `-- receiver deduplicates by delivery ID
        `-- exhausted -> dead-letter queue

examples.title: Module boundary
examples.diversityRationale: Groups a module by public contract and hidden mechanisms, crosses that boundary with an explicit dependency, and keeps most leaves compact.
examples.ascii:
[M] Template engine
|-- Public contract
|   |-- compile(text): Template
|   `-- render(template, bindings): text
|-- Internal machinery
|   |-- parser -> syntax tree
|   |-- compiler -> rendering instructions
|   `-- interpreter
|       `-- [D] instructions + bindings -> output text
`-- Extension boundary
    `-- registered formatters: value -> text
        `-- interpreter calls them; parser stays private

examples.title: Event fan-out
examples.diversityRationale: Independent reactions to one event; explicitly avoids implying sibling order or treating every consequence as a nested call.
examples.ascii:
DocumentSaved(documentId, revision)
|-- Search subscriber -> enqueue reindex
|-- Preview subscriber -> invalidate cached thumbnail
`-- Audit subscriber -> append revision record

Subscribers run independently; branch order is not execution order.
Each subscriber handles its own retry.
